newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangdong Inv considers more spinoffs.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Inv considers more spinoffs.

text.p: Guangdong Investment Ltd said on Thursday it would continue to acquire and invest in quality assets and spin off more units with strong growth potential.

"The directors are considering separate listings of more companies within the group that possess great potential for further development in order to expedite its growth amid keen market competition," chairman He Keqin said in a statement.
The company spun off its leather unit Guangdong Tannery Ltd in December 1996. The unit's initial public offer (IPO) was subscribed 667 times, setting a new record for IPOs in Hong Kong, it said.
"The group will continue to acquire and invest in quality assets to broaden its earnings base," he said in the company's earnings statement.

Guangdong Investment announced on Wednesday that it posted 4.4 percent growth in net profit to HK$604.29 million ($78 million) in 1996, including an exceptional gain of HK$83.85 million from dilution of its shareholding in a subsidiary, interest from a subsidiary's IPO and sale of a joint venture.
Turnover fell to HK$6.47 billion from HK$8.19 billion, and earnings per share also decreased to HK$0.28 from HK$0.29.

The company's directors also recommended a bonus issue of one warrant for every 10 shares held. Each warrant would give its holder the right to buy one company share at HK$8 each, subject to adjustment, on or before July 30, 1999.
"The group benefits from the easy access to investment opportunities in Guangdong and other provinces by maintaining a close relation with Guangdong Provincial government," it said.
The company said it would continue to develop its core businesses, particularly in infrastructure investment and industrial manufacturing in 1997.
Guangdong Investment is also engaged in travel services and hotel operations, property investment and development, and retail and general merchandise business.
